unlock_condition.description: Sidon is the destination of the tutorial quest — unlocked naturally

tile_details.description: limestone paving, slightly newer and more uniform than Tyre
walls have embedded coloured glass fragments that catch light
heavy cedar doors with bronze merchant guild seals
narrow covered street lined with competing merchant stalls

night.glass_quarter_note: Glass embedded in walls faintly glows blue at night from moonlight

location.lore_note: Sidon was once greater than Tyre. It still believes it is. The city has a chip on its shoulder — merchants here are aggressive, competitive, and proud. Prices are slightly better than Tyre for crafted goods but the guilds are controlling and suspicious of outsiders.

visual.description: Larger than Kefr-Yamm, smaller than Tyre. Two docks, a warehouse, a harbor fee booth.
Open-front workshop with a furnace visible from the street. Finished glass objects displayed on wooden shelves outside. The air near the entrance is hot.

buildings.note: Glass beads are unique to Sidon. In West Africa and distant kingdoms they are worth far more than their Sidon price — a key early trade arbitrage opportunity.

visual.description: An imposing two-story building with bronze guild seals on every pillar. Guards at the door check who enters. Inside: a hall of merchants arguing over contracts, maps on the walls, a scales room.

services.benefit: 10% better buy prices at all Sidonian shops. Required for Guild quests.

services.description: Registers a guaranteed buy/sell deal with a named merchant — locks in a price for 7 days

faction.note: Gaining reputation with Sidon's guild creates tension with Tyre's guild — they are rivals

visual.description: A narrow covered street with stalls pressed together on both sides. More chaotic and louder than Tyre's Grand Bazaar but with better deals if you haggle.

haggle_mechanic.description: Sidon is the only location with a haggling mini-game. Player can attempt to lower buy prices.

rival_merchant_event.description: A rival merchant NPC begins appearing and always buys the item the player is trying to sell just before the player gets to the stall — driving the price down

visual.description: Sidon's god of healing. A calmer, quieter temple than Tyre's Melqart. Built on the highest point of the city. Pilgrims and sick people come here from far away.

special_mechanic.description: Sick or injured NPCs travel to this temple. The player can help them (bring medicine from other locations) for reputation rewards and unique lore dialogue.

lines.speaker: baalshamin
lines.text: You must be the one Dagon sent. Good. I've been waiting. Hand over the package — here's your receipt.

lines.speaker: baalshamin
lines.text: Tell Dagon the Sidon price on rope has gone up. He'll want to know.

lines.speaker: baalshamin
lines.text: Back again. Good. Sidon treats returning merchants better than strangers. What are you buying or selling?

lines.speaker: eshmunazar
lines.text: Kefr-Yamm. I know where that is. Barely. What makes you think you belong in this hall?

player_choices.text: Name the merchants you've dealt with

secret.description: Is secretly negotiating a trade agreement with Tyre's Dye Guild behind his own guild's back — a betrayal that would ruin him if exposed.

mechanic.description: Appears after player's 3rd market visit. Always seems to buy what the player wants just before the player gets there. Not hostile — he finds it funny. Can become an ally or a proper rival depending on player choices.

lines.speaker: hiram_minor
lines.text: Oh — were you going to buy that perfume? Shame. Maybe next time.

entry_position.description: Behind the oldest furnace in the glass quarter — a wall that looks solid but has a hidden door, detectable only when the furnace is cold at night

discovery_triggers.description: Glassblower mentions the workshops were built over something older
At night with furnaces cold, a faint draft is noticeable near the oldest furnace

options.description: Door only detectable when furnace is cold at night

contents.description: Pre-Phoenician stone tunnels running under the glass quarter. Walls are scorched black from ancient fires.
Fragments of glass older than Sidonian glassmaking — suggesting someone else discovered glass here first

loot.description: Second piece of the Map of the Outer Sea. Shows islands north of the known world.

steps.note: Glass beads are unknown in Cyprus — price is 4x Sidon buy price

reward.note: Reward is the profit margin itself, not a fixed silver reward

options.description: Keep a copy and use it to blackmail Eshmunazar later
Reveal his secret negotiations to the full guild

expose_eshmunazar.note: Eshmunazar is removed. A new, friendlier guild master takes over.

steps.description: Find out who Hiram the Quick really is and who he works for

options.description: Help Hiram pay off his debt — he becomes a trade ally
Report him to the guild — he loses his market access
Out-trade him publicly — winner takes the better market stall

befriend_hiram.description: Hiram tips player about good deals across 3 cities

economy.note: Sidon prices are slightly better than Tyre for crafted goods but slightly worse for raw materials. The guild membership is the main economic advantage here.
